#### [A frameshift mutation in PRICKLE1 causes skeletal dysplasia in Cheviot sheep](<https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.07.757262>)
*Oswald Matika, Megan G Davey, Jorge del Pozo, Heather A Finlayson, Colin Farquharson, Denis J Headon, James W Kijas, Lynn McTeir, Cameron Bathos-Samblas, Elizabeth Watson, Valentina Riggio, Jeffrey J Schoenebeck, Tobias Schwarz, Katherine Ann Staines, Ricardo Pong-Wong, Zen H Lu, Stephen C Bishop, John A Woolliams, Alan L Archibald* <br>
A recessive 10-base-pair deletion in the *PRICKLE1* gene causes a severe developmental syndrome in South Country Cheviot sheep characterized by skeletal deformities, neural tube defects, and polycystic kidneys, leading to the creation of a commercial DNA test to eliminate the disease from flocks.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Polarization of the Drosophila oocyte by active cortical exchange](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10916v1>)
*Mohammadhossein Firouznia, Wen Lu, Margot Lakonishok, Reza Farhadifar, Vladimir I. Gelfand, Michael J. Shelley* <br>
*oskar* ribonucleoprotein particles achieve stable posterior localization through a balance of position-dependent cortical exchange and cytoplasmic diffusion that prevents their intrinsic self-attraction from causing irreversible phase separation.
:::
